name: Shared numeric, prose, merged and nested table layouts
accept: Read native data, prose, code and composed API tables. Every column sizes from its actual body content independently of the header's semantic role: short values remain compact, prose and long lists receive reading room, code scrolls locally, and new child content updates sizing. Check long text under Name, Type, Value, Required and unknown headings as well as short text under Description. Short numeric lists must not inherit a prose width floor. Native merged headers and totals remain unchanged, nested tables plan independently, and wide tables scroll locally to their final column. Compare desktop/tablet/phone, both themes and original source text and links. Density does not imply a fixed layout. Include ordinary landing, quick-start and billing pages outside API route names.

name: Compact required columns in parameter tables
accept: Read three-, four- and five-column parameter tables. Required/optional flags are centered in a compact column identified by its header, including when that column is first or third. Short headers remain on one line; longer conditions stay readable. On the custom-tool page switch Go, Python, TypeScript and RESTful API for both GET and POST descriptions. Descriptions retain their readable width and tables scroll locally at narrow viewports. Numeric/pricing columns retain authored alignment, and native merged cells retain their spans. Include aliases 是否必选, 是否必需, 必选 and configuration/name headers; read 填写要求 with 视场景 and 建议填写 without splitting those phrases.

name: Code tabs with a shared frame and toolbar
accept: Language and package-manager code tabs use one outer frame with wrap/copy controls on the tab row. A repeated language caption is omitted; SDK/platform labels retain their distinct code language and explicit filenames remain visible. At narrow widths, scroll the tab row and code locally without overlapping the controls or widening the page. Switch using mouse and arrow keys, toggle wrapping, and copy each selected sample with its original whitespace. Verify that mixed prose tabs retain their content and independent code controls.

name: OpenAPI nested schema and examples
accept: Click field names and padding, expand/collapse all, touch a nested field, Tab/Enter, switch example language and response status. Targets >=44 CSS px; both locales offer the same controls. On speech-to-text join, body and example status labels both read 非 200 / Non-200 for the default response; switching preserves error content and original response-default anchors. Do not label a default-only response or a default with multiple explicit statuses as non-200. On query-user-status, parameters without a source type must not gain a placeholder type label; preserve names, required status, descriptions and links. Declared types and authored aliases remain visible.

name: Tables, callouts and code tabs
accept: Read DELETE and 100/second; read long descriptions and nested callouts. Scroll to the final column locally. Switch all three installation tab groups with click and arrow keys; rounded frames remain intact. In shared documentation and API code blocks, toggle wrapping on and off with mouse and keyboard: long lines fit locally when wrapped, horizontal scrolling returns when unwrapped, line numbers and highlighting remain, and copied code retains its original whitespace. Check the localized pressed state, caller actions and independent state of two blocks.

name: Authored MDX and platform navigation
accept: Open the mobile TOC, jump to a real member, use Back, and read its parameters and code. Heading remains visible below the sticky navigation.

name: TypeDoc overloads and notices
accept: Match each of the three overloads to its own signature, parameters and return value. Compatibility and HTTPS notices retain their structure and meaning. Long Promise/tuple return types wrap in their cell, retain every type link, and leave the description readable at compact widths. Optional/Readonly are signature metadata, not part of the member heading; property declarations use the native signature frame. Nested object fields are ordinary lists in their parent cell, without independent cards. Explicit notices use standard callouts without quotation marks or italic text; actual quotations remain quotes. Verify that legacy TypeDoc attention blocks use caution callouts and deprecated metadata retains its original destination inside a standard notice. Type-only returns preserve void, Promise<void> and linked types without an empty description table. Read a long signature with wrapping on and off, follow a visibly identifiable type link, and distinguish modifier badges and adjacent member boundaries.

name: Oxygen parameter lists
accept: Both historical fragments navigate correctly; description bullets, numbering and nesting are visible and distinct from possible-value badges.

name: Doxygen Android Whiteboard
accept: Table headers name parameters rather than source paths. Read member details and navigate a real type link. Summary tables have no decorative blank rows or visible anchor URLs. Inherited destinations still work, spans remain native table cells, and introductory prose stays unchanged.

name: Appledoc Objective-C names and tables
accept: Keep valid Objective-C -/+ markers and Declared In metadata. A plain .h label need not be a link. Real type links work; four-column descriptions stay readable via local scrolling.

name: DITA structures
accept: Structure members, signatures and descriptions remain associated. Long identifiers wrap or scroll without widening the entire page.

name: Legacy authored REST reference
accept: Read long request and response sections, follow TOC links and horizontally scroll long code within its frame.

name: API entries and legacy navigation
accept: Navigate from the API entry through a product and version. External SDK current-version links and historical entry links have correct destinations; external templates are outside this repo's fix scope. From a C++ enum, click the RTC product breadcrumb to its filtered catalog and the platform ancestor to its real overview; use Back to return.

name: English Whiteboard local links
accept: Follow conversion and deprecated-reference links. Both resolve to the intended language and page; cross-page anchors remain valid.

name: Shared styles across languages
accept: Compare the same endpoint in both locales in light/dark and a narrow viewport. Behavior and spacing agree; only translated text and intentional product differences vary. On agent history, read the overview-to-first-section transition: where a shared overview precedes a separate documentation column, its first group must not stack a full chapter margin on the existing grid gap. Check authorization and parameter-first variants, including an overview ending in a callout: terminal outer margins reset without removing internal callout padding. Later chapter spacing and the mobile view switch remain distinct.

name: Authored language and syntax highlighting
accept: Programming-language fences show real syntax tokens in both themes; known API prototypes carry their SDK language. Plain output stays plain. Language captions, code values and copy behavior agree with the authored source.

name: Native parameter tables and linked signature frames
accept: Parameter and return lists use the ordinary native DocsTable scroll surface. Signature frames match ordinary Fumadocs code frames. Type links and modifiers remain on the same native code line in the same monospace font; copy excludes metadata labels, and type links plus historical parameter anchors still resolve. Imported linked-signature content is absent from English; verify its shared module with bilingual component fixtures. Follow the historical watermarkUrl anchor. Its description starts with the first visible paragraph, without anchor-induced top spacing. Body row headings and descriptions share the row surface in both themes.
